steps.text: Whisk flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, ginger, and cinnamon in a bowl; set aside. Beat egg, vanilla, and molasses in a separate mixing bowl until smooth. Whisk in water until completely incorporated. Stir flour mixture into molasses mixture until just combined (a few lumps are okay).

Heat a lightly oiled griddle over medium-high heat. Drop batter by large spoonfuls onto the griddle, and cook until bubbles form and the edges are dry. Flip, and cook until browned on the other side. Repeat with remaining batter.

raw_recipe.headline: Grandma's Gingerbread Pancakes
raw_recipe.description: These easy gingerbread pancakes are made with molasses and spiced with ginger and cinnamon to taste just like gingerbread!

review.reviewBody: I read through the reviews very carefully before making this, which I think was my first mistake. I usually don't do that and fly by the seat of my shorts. I doubled the recipe so I could freeze some for busy mornings, added more baking powder for a fluffier pancake, doubled the spices and added nutmeg and allspice and I cut the water down to two cups, as a lot of people mentioned that the batter was way too wet. My pancakes were pretty thick and fluffy but they were a pain to cook. The spices I doubled and added were perfect, it's just that maybe cutting back the liquid to two cups was too much? Next time, I'll cut it back only a half cup and I think it might be perfect. It really does need the extra baking powder for a fluffier pancake. That being said, tasty pancake. Even with my flub-up's, this recipe made 15 large pancakes when doubled. Out of the 15, I had three leftover. My boys loved them. I had a small bite of one and thought it was mighty tasty. My son actually remarked that "these are the best pancakes EVER, Mom".

I did as the reviews suggested and made some changes to the recipe to fit my personal pancake tastes: decrease the water to 1 cup, increase the ginger to 1 tsp, increase the cinnamon to 2 tsp, and increase the baking powder to 1-1/2 tsp. I also cooked them with butter instead of oil (butter is always the better choice!). They didn't turn out looking the best, but that's my fault - I don't exactly have the most steady of hands when there's coffee in my system. They were also a bit undercooked, but that's also my fault, as I poured a bit too much batter on the griddle and then didn't cook them long enough as I was afraid of burning them. All in all, these are the best pancakes I have ever made - or had! I will definitely be making these for the family when we celebrate an early Christmas in a couple of weeks! Thanks Grammie for the delicious recipe!

I looked at the reviews and looked at some of the pictures. I ended up following the recipe, except for the water. I used 1 1/4 cup of water. I don't use oil because I use a non stick griddle. To measure out I used a 1/3 cup measuring cup so they would all be the same size. With this recipe, I made 11 pancakes. When I make pancakes I hate runny batter and I hate a doughy batter as well, so with that in mind I used a small spatula to slightly spread them.

These pancakes are delicious! I made them for Christmas morning and the family loved them. After reading the other reviews, I made some changes and they turned out perfect. I doubled the recipe, increased the baking powder to 1 tablespoon and reduced the water by 1/2 cup. Makes the kitchen smell wonderful and is a perfect Christmas breakfast!

I really dislike it when people change a recipe and then give it a review as if they made it as written. That being said,...guilty as charged, but I didn't change the flavor profile just the structural issues. The ingredients and amounts didn't look right to me, which was confirmed with what I read in the reviews. So what I did was eliminated the baking soda (activates with acidic ingredients, none present), upped the baking powder to 3tsp (fixed the "flat pancake complaint) reduced the total liquid from 1+3/4 ( 1 1/2 water 1/4molasses ) to 1+1/2 (1 1/4 water 1/4molasses) to fix the runny batter issue.

I have made this recipe many times over the past few years and it comes out better with the following modifications: 2 tsp baking powder, double the amount of the spices and add 1/4 tsp cloves, cut back to 1 cup or 1 1/4 cup of water depending on how thick you like your pancakes, and make sure you grease the pan every one to two pancakes otherwise the stick very bad. This will give you fluffier pancakes that actually have a decent but not overwhelming amount of flavor.

To make theses vegan I substituted the egg for 1 tbsp ground flax seed and 3 tbsp water. Let sit for a few minutes to thicken up. I was hesitant to add the 1 1/2 cups water, so I started with 1 cup. The first batch were really thick so I added the remaining water and made sure the pancakes were thinner. Absolutely delicious! serve with maple syrup. Ensure you use non-GMO products, to make this 'truly' vegan. Thank your grandmother for me!

This is a good base but I wouldn't recommend following to a T.
I modified it with the following:
Instead of water, I changed it to Buttermilk
Added an additional 1/4 tsp vanilla extract
Added 2 tbsp brown sugar
After mixing ingredients, it was too runny and added an additional 3 tbsp of flour.

I was surprised that there was no fat added to batter, but proceeded to follow the written directions. . . I trust Sarah Jo, so I added an extra 1/4 tsp. of baking powder. I used 1/2 c. of water, stirred, added 1/2 c. of keifer, stirred, added 1/4 c. of water, stirred, and PERFECT consistency. (I’m always looking for a way to use my keifer). This made 8 1/3 cup pancakes. *1 cup white flour, 1/2 cup wheat* I had mine with canned peach pie filling and vanilla yogurt. The texture was a bit “tough.” Fat needed? Spices were subtle. BASICALLY, just OK.

Good basic recipe. My grandmother may have just spoiled me, but I've always believed that pancakes should be able to stand alone, not smothered in syrup. I, like other reviewers, like a fluffy pancake. So I only used 1 c water. Added 1Tbsp sugar. Used 2 tsp cinnamon, 2tsp ginger & 1/4 tsp clove, for bite. For my taste they turned out perfect. Note, since the batter will be thicker, you will need to spread it around a bit on your griddle. Enjoy!

I gave these four stars only because I feel that the comments and changes that resulted from reading them helped make this such a delicious treat. I cut the water buy a fourth after doubling the recipe and I did and Ace Kos more ginger and cinnamon As well as baking powder. The trick that was the toughest with these pancakes was juggling the temperature of the pan so it wasn’t too hot nor too cool. 

 They tend to cook rather quickly and burn fast if you don’t keep a watchful eye on them. Be careful not to overcook. Because of the consistency of the batter, I did not seem to have a problem with Call cooked on the outside Ross bites on the inside and as long as I balanced. The pay off was AMAZING! Very tasty pancakes! I only wish we had the time to make gingerbread men out of them as we had planned. They would be adorable.

I do have to say that I enjoy a little more salt in the batter to balance the suite. That might come though, from salted butter if you use it. We presented ours with powdered sugar sprinkled on top and it made for A beautifully festive plate to bring to a potluck. Not sure how well the pancakes held up to the rewarm but they were already to mini quiche being offered up by other people. LOL this would be a wonderful Christmas time treat for kids.

Delicious. Next time will add flour as suggested as the batter was wet. My fault for not following recommendations. However, I wanted to try it just as recipe read for the first time. Hubbie and brother in law love them. Definitely will make again. This wound be a great Christmas or Thanksgiving morning breakfast along with some maple candied bacon. Yum!!! Thanks so much! If I do any tweaks I will come back and add later. I love them as is tho. And I used a cast iron flat skillet with a lil bit of butter. Fabulous!

This is delicious and I don't know why it isn't rated higher. It is a nice holiday treat for our family and goes well with real maple syrup. I make it at least once a year during the holiday season. I prefer these over actually gingerbread cookies because the lightness of pancakes, and they are tender as well.
Very unique and delicious taste.

Followed the recipe exactly. Should have listened to my little voice. Much to thin. Added almost another cup, abd extea ginger. Made the pancakes rubbery and low flavor. Were I making crêpes, the consistency would've been perfect, not for pancakes
I love these anytime of year!Thank you for sharing this recipe!
The gingerbread flavor was a little lackluster, and the batter was definitely too watery. I probably added an extra cup and a half of flour to get the right consistency
I doubled the recipe, but added another 1/2 cup flour, and only 2 cups of water.
They turned out so well!! Definitely going to make these again.

I liked the taste although there is either WAY TOO MUCH water in the recipe or not enough flour. Following directions it came out so runny it wasn't funny. added almost another cup of flour before it even came close to the consistency of pancake batter. Is it possible you accidentally put a "1" in front of the 1/2 cup of water by accident? I think next time I do try this I will start with a half cup of water and see if that is enough.
